questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to stay visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell drivers what rules they must follow.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help reduce crash risk?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible and signal your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch for hazards ahead. Never rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: Why might you drift into another lane during a curve?

options.text: You are taking the turn too fast.
You don't know how to steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: If you enter a curve too fast, you may cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should NOT do what?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Never brake suddenly.

questions.question: How can you help a driver merging from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane; it is not your responsibility.
Move to a lane away from the entrance ramp if you can.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane away from the entrance ramp if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging drivers plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to make room for them.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid, causing loss of control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens?

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Don't use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: Stay visible and signal your moves. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid sudden hazards.

questions.question: What should your passenger do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean the same way you lean. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When braking on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes harder than usual.
Apply the brakes more gently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use extra caution and apply the brakes gently.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up so each rider can go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a specific spot later.

questions.question: To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on all the time.
Ride in the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on all the time.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Wear bright and reflective clothing. Change your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who do not have much experience.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and next to you. You may see a little of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to stay out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, and have an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers do not try to share your lane with you.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra alert when another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Cannot usually be heard by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so others may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Set them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane beside you.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Always replace a helmet after it has been in a crash.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Tighten your hold on the handle grips and increase your speed to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to correct the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.
